I partnered with them on this thread, so this is paid for, but sincere: I use them myself. You can get 20% off DeleteMe at joindeleteme.com/Wolfers with code WOLFERS.
A service like DeleteMe can give you back some of that ownership. They file removal requests with hundreds of brokers on your behalf and keep at it when your data reappears.

The fix Varian predicted: when bargaining is costly, hire an agent. Songwriters use collecting societies; you can use a removal service.
The twist: he imagined you'd get paid for your data. Instead, you pay to claw it back. First grabber keeps the entitlement.

So a market grew in the gap: data brokers scrape your name, address, and old hotmail account, then sell it to anyone with a credit card.
Notice who's missing from that transaction: YOU. Nobody asks, pays, or consults you. The result? 4 billion robocalls a month.

In theory: you should own your data like a songwriter owns a song. Spotify needs a license to stream it, a dog food ad needs a separate one.
In practice: transaction costs kill this. You can't negotiate with 10,000 data brokers. Nobody pays enough to make it worth your morning.
